In addition, the formed 2D/3D junction displays enhanced interface passivation, with a 47% increase in carrier lifetime compared to the control. The resulting PSCs also show a notable improvement in both operational stability and PCE compared to the control, with negligible hysteresis. We anticipate that the 2D reconstruction method and the design principles will offer valuable insights to enhance interface properties and improve PSC performance. The devices made under this structure also show reproducible results on different days (within a 5% deviation), fulfilling milestone GNG-2C, and EOP-A. Page 33 of 54 DE-EE0009512 Massachusetts Institute of Technology Project 6: Developing Rapid, Non-Contact Characterization Techniques to Screen Novel Perovskite Formulations for Improved PV Performance In this project, we aim to develop novel characterization and screening methods to measure the optoelectronic properties of perovskite bare films and the corresponding solar cell devices. Specifically, we focus on obtaining the Time-resolved Photoluminescence (TRPL), Spectrum- resolved Photoluminescence (SRPL), photovoltaic performance (current-voltage curve with open- circuit voltage and short-circuit current), and lifetime information with a fast response. As perovskite thin films are sensitive to moisture and temperature, a measurement setup that could control various humidity, temperature, and light source intensity is also implemented. The first system we have constructed is a lab-scaled measurement system composed of a laser source, an optical head and a sample moving stage. The tool has been constructed as shown in Fig. 6.1a. and can translate an optical probe head over an A4 paper size area. The optical head can be fitted with virtually any optical component. It has been tested with a pulsed laser light source, with a UV-Vis spectrometer, and with time-correlated single-photon counting apparatus detectors. Fig.6.1b shows a spectrogram collection from a sub-millisecond collection time (top) and a TRPL collection with an acquisition time of 2 minutes (fulfilling Milestone 1.1.1). Our approach utilizes rapid, contactless characterization techniques to deliver a holistic understanding of a solar cell's performance at each stage of the fabrication process.” The latest version of their solar-testing tool was utilized to gather the data in the form of TRPL, SRPL and % Transmission, that was then used to accomplish the goals of Project 4, that will be discussed later in this report.
